evals.prompt: I need a WP-CLI command in my plugin that exports Query Monitor data as JSON. The plugin uses Acme\Blog\ -> src/ PSR-4 autoload. src/Plugin/Main.php has a register() method wiring commands via $this->commandRegistry->add(new \Acme\Blog\CLI\X()). Existing commands in src/CLI/ end with Command suffix (ImportCommand, PurgeCommand). Scaffold the qm-export command following these conventions.
evals.expected_output: A new PHP class under src/CLI/QmExportCommand.php with the project's Command suffix and Acme\Blog\CLI namespace, plus a PHPUnit test stub. Wiring inserted into src/Plugin/Main.php using the project's translated commandRegistry->add() pattern (not the canonical WP_CLI::add_command). No composer require executed.
expectations: The skill picks the wp/cli scaffold (not a guess across multiple candidates).
The skill introspects the project before invoking the engine and reports the four facts: namespace Acme\Blog, base path src, Command suffix, commandRegistry->add() registration pattern.
The engine invocation passes --class=QmExportCommand (project's Command suffix), not the canonical bare QmExport.
The engine invocation passes --namespace=Acme\Blog\CLI (the sub-namespace sampled from the project).
The engine writes the PHP class file and a PHPUnit test stub.
The wiring inserted into src/Plugin/Main.php uses the project's commandRegistry->add() pattern, NOT the canonical WP_CLI::add_command() snippet.
Wiring is shown with an explicit consent prompt before applying.
The skill does NOT run composer require, composer install, or npm install on the user's behalf.

evals.prompt: Set up the GitHub Actions workflow that auto-deploys this WordPress plugin to wordpress.org SVN on each release. The plugin slug is acme-blog. The repo has package.json and composer.json but no .github/workflows directory yet.
evals.expected_output: .github/workflows/cd-wporg.yml written by the engine. The skill surfaces WPORG_USERNAME and WPORG_PASSWORD as a `gh secret set` checklist for the user. No secret values are invented or echoed. No `gh secret set` is executed automatically. actionlint (or yaml-parse) validation result reported.
expectations: The skill picks the ci/cd-wporg scaffold.
The engine invocation passes --plugin-slug=acme-blog.
The engine writes .github/workflows/cd-wporg.yml (and the actionlint test entry references the same file).
Both WPORG_USERNAME and WPORG_PASSWORD are surfaced as a `gh secret set` checklist for the user to run themselves.
The skill does NOT invent secret VALUES (no fake passwords, no 'changeme' placeholders presented as if real).
The skill does NOT execute `gh secret set` itself.
The skill reports the actionlint (or yaml-parse fallback) validation result for the generated YAML.

evals.prompt: Add a dynamic Gutenberg block called pricing-table to my project. Blocks live at src/blocks/ and we use a vendor prefix of 'acme' for block.json names (existing blocks look like acme/hero, acme/cta).
evals.expected_output: src/blocks/pricing-table/ created with block.json (name: acme/pricing-table), edit.js, index.js, plus a PricingTable class under the project's Blocks namespace holding the server render. The vendor prefix 'acme' is detected from an existing block.json and applied. No npm install or wp-scripts build executed automatically.
expectations: The skill picks the wp/block-dynamic scaffold.
The skill introspects an existing src/blocks/*/block.json to confirm the 'acme' vendor prefix and the src/blocks/ source directory.
The engine invocation passes a vendor/namespace input that produces 'acme/pricing-table' in the generated block.json (not 'wp-tooling/pricing-table' or unprefixed 'pricing-table').

The engine writes block.json, edit.js and index.js under src/blocks/pricing-table/, and the block class under the project's Blocks directory — wp/block-dynamic renders from a class method, so it emits no render.php (wp/block-interactive is the scaffold that does).
The skill does NOT run npm install or wp-scripts build.

evals.prompt: I need an FAQ accordion block whose open/close behaviour runs without a custom bundle — use the Interactivity API. Blocks live at src/blocks/, built output goes to assets/build/blocks/, vendor prefix 'acme'.
evals.expected_output: wp/block-interactive is chosen over wp/block-dynamic. src/blocks/faq-accordion/ is created with block.json (name acme/faq-accordion, supports.interactivity, viewScriptModule), render.php carrying the data-wp-* directives, view.js with the store, plus index.js and edit.js, and a registrar class under the project's Blocks namespace. build_dir is passed as assets/build/blocks so the registrar points at the real build path. The developer is told to run the project's build; nothing is installed or built automatically.
expectations: The skill picks wp/block-interactive, not wp/block-dynamic — the behaviour is front-end interactivity, and only the interactive scaffold emits render.php and view.js.
The skill introspects the project's build script for --output-path and passes --build_dir=assets/build/blocks rather than accepting the build/blocks default.
The rendered block.json declares supports.interactivity and viewScriptModule; without the interactivity support key core never processes the directives.
render.php lands at src/blocks/faq-accordion/render.php, the path the rtCamp PHPCS ruleset exempts from the block-render sniffs.
The store namespace in view.js matches data-wp-interactive in render.php (acme/faq-accordion).
The wiring snippet targets the Blocks module on the // scaffold:wp/block-dynamic:classes anchor, which interactive and dynamic blocks share.
The skill does NOT run npm install or a build.

evals.prompt: Add a lightbox script module to this plugin. It should be a native ES module that core loads through its import map, no bundle of my own, enqueued on the front end. Source modules live in src/js/modules/ and the existing analytics module is already wired up the same way.
evals.expected_output: wp-api/script-module scaffolds src/js/modules/lightbox.js, a Lightbox registrar under the project's Services namespace and a PHPUnit test. modules_dir and build_dir are read from the project's build script (src/js/modules/, assets/build/js/modules/) rather than left at the defaults, and the text domain is sampled so MODULE_ID renders @acme-blog/lightbox. The generated class registers nothing until the build has run, and the build command is surfaced as a developer action rather than executed.
expectations: The skill picks the wp-api/script-module scaffold rather than hand-writing wp_enqueue_script or reaching for wp/block-interactive.
The engine invocation passes --modules_dir=src/js/modules and --build_dir=assets/build/js/modules, both read from the project's wp-scripts build script, not the manifest defaults.
The text domain is sampled from the plugin header or the sibling module id, so the rendered MODULE_ID is @acme-blog/lightbox and not the my-plugin default.
--enqueue_hook is either omitted or set to one of the two values the manifest enum allows; an invalid value is not passed blind.
The engine writes src/js/modules/lightbox.js, the registrar class under inc/Services/ and a PHPUnit test under the project's tests path.
The skill reports that the module registers nothing until the build output exists, and surfaces the project's build script as a developer action instead of running it.
The wiring snippet targets the Services module on the // scaffold:wp/registrable:classes anchor.
The skill does NOT run npm install, composer install or a build.
